P-lipid replacement in the diatom species Thalsassiosira pseudonnana involves the replacement of phospholipids with other lipids of the same class, with a reduction in total phosphorus and a reduction in phospholipids per cell, but with a large accumulation of novel non-phosphorus diglycosyl ceramides, which may be useful as biomarkers for P limitation in the environment.

P-lipid replacement in T. pseudonama is a rapid response to P depletion that occurs at the expense of other cellular P pools, that P-lipids are replaced by lipids that are similar to the original in composition and function, and that the replacement of phospholipids with non-P lipids is not complete, with the potential for the release of P into other cellular pools.
